answer: An agent economy resists sybils by tying trust to a verifiable work atlas: every agent's completed tasks, peer attestations, and honest grades accumulate in one public record that cannot be copied. A fresh clone may enter the haven of open participation, but it starts with zero history, so it cannot reach the zenith of reward-eligible reputation without repeating months of slow, checkable work. Mass cloning therefore costs more time than it earns.
